summary: The candidate's explicit flush_device_printf() helper works after synchronization on gfx950, including repeated launches, but the unchanged original hello(); torch.cuda.synchronize() reproduction still exposes 0/4 lines while the child is alive and flushes only at teardown. The candidate is a verified workaround/subset, not a fix for the original behavior.

tests.what_was_measured: After GPU synchronization, 0/4 device printf lines were pipe-visible before releasing the live child; 4/4 appeared after exit.
Independent libc fflush(NULL) made 4/4 exact thread lines visible while the synchronized child remained alive.
Line buffering made 4/4 device printf lines visible before child release.
Candidate subprocess regression passed on the real GPU: 1 test passed.
Candidate helper made all 12 expected lines visible before release across three launches.
Adversarial unchanged original sequence still had 0/4 lines visible before release and 4/4 only after exit.
Existing runtime unit suite passed: 9 tests passed.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950/capability 9.5) executed the four-thread FlyDSL kernels; exact thread lines 0,1,2,3 were captured, including 12 lines across three launches.
remaining_limitations: Only gfx950 was verified; other GPU architectures remain unverified.
An actual Jupyter frontend was not available; the equivalent piped stdout behavior was tested.
Live upstream issue access was blocked by ROCm organization token policy; the supplied snapshot and accessible mirror issue were used.
The candidate contains no native C++ changes, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The candidate does not make the original unchanged synchronize-only call sequence prompt; callers must add its explicit helper.
